report:
# Research Summary: Acupuncture for Depression During Pregnancy

**Bottom line: The claim has modest, mixed support — promising but not conclusive.**

The strongest direct evidence comes from a Stanford-led RCT (Manber et al., 2010, *Obstetrics & Gynecology*) of 150 pregnant women meeting DSM-IV criteria for major depression. Participants received either depression-specific acupuncture, control (non-specific) acupuncture, or massage. After 8 weeks, the depression-specific acupuncture group showed a 63% response rate (≥50% symptom reduction) versus 44% in the combined comparison groups, and lower Hamilton Depression scores overall (https://med.stanford.edu/news/all-news/2010/02/acupuncture-lessens-depression-symptoms-during-pregnancy-study-shows.html; https://journals.lww.com/greenjournal/fulltext/2010/03000/acupuncture_for_depression_during_pregnancy__a.7.aspx). This built on an earlier smaller pilot by the same team (Manber et al., 2004) that also found symptom reduction.

However, this remains largely a single research group's small trial base, and other researchers have called findings only "preliminary" and "suggestive," calling for more rigorous confirmation (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4758005/). A follow-up feasibility study (AcuAnteDep) explicitly noted limitations of conventional treatments but stressed more research was needed rather than confirming efficacy (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0165032720302081).

Skeptics note a broader problem across acupuncture research: sham/control acupuncture groups often show substantial improvement too, suggesting nonspecific or placebo effects, and that "control acupuncture" may not be truly inert (https://theness.com/neurologicablog/why-i-am-skeptical-of-acupuncture/).

**Conclusion:** Evidence suggests acupuncture may help reduce depressive symptoms in pregnancy, but sample sizes are small, replication is limited, and blinding/placebo issues weaken certainty. It's reasonable as a complementary option, not yet a proven standalone treatment.
